messages:
Alice (PM): quick sync — customer X asked for a paid "priority routing" add-on that guarantees per-route P95 < 120ms for 99% of requests. can we scope?
Ben (Eng): interesting. need clarity: is this a latency SLA, or a routing priority that increases capacity?
Carlos (Sales): customer expects both: lower latency and higher effective throughput during peak. they'd pay +15% on top of reserved capacity.
Dana (Finance): +15% sounds vague. we need per-unit pricing and how it scales with committed GPUs and qps.
Alice (PM): draft constraints: - applies only to Dedicated and Private - opt-in per-application route - soft-flow control + emergency fallback to standard tier.
Ben (Eng): constraints matter: we can implement a QoS queue that tags VIP requests and routes to warm pools. need autoscale buffer and KV cache pinning.
Frank-bot: deploy note: previous warm-pool experiment caused 6% higher idle GPU hours in staging. see /ops/logs/7001
Carlos (Sales): customers will accept some cap if we offer a credit mechanism for missed SLOs. proposal: credit = 2x monthly addon fee for any month with >1% SLO breach.
Evie (Legal): credits are fine but watch for continuous liability. need to limit aggregate credits and define measurement windows. recommend max credit = 50% of addon revenue per contract term.
Dana (Finance): agree with cap. also require telemetry to calculate credits programmatically. billing integration work estimate?
Ben (Eng): billing hook is small. main work: routing policy, warm pool orchestration, per-tenant metrics and long-tail analysis. estimate 6-8 sprints for MLP.
Alice (PM): launch criteria brainstorm: 1) end-to-end e2e test showing p95 <120ms for 95% of routes in staging; 2) billing + credit automation; 3) docs + sales playbook; 4) legal addendum template.
Carlos (Sales): add: a pilot with 2 customers (one enterprise, one scale-up) + success criteria: sustained latency under target and <1.5x cost uplift.
Ben (Eng): technical risk: multi-tenant warm pools may increase tail latencies for non-VIP. need isolation rules or dedicated warm pools per customer tier.
Alice (PM): decision point — do we require dedicated warm pools for Tier-1 customers, or rely on priority tagging? tradeoffs documented below.
Alice (PM): Tradeoff A: priority tagging + shared warm pools => +faster rollout, lower infra cost, higher tail risk for standard users.
Alice (PM): Tradeoff B: per-customer warm pools => higher infra cost, stronger isolation, simpler SLO math for credits.
Dana (Finance): run a cost model for both: include idle GPU cost, amortized over expected addon revenue.
Ben (Eng): quick numbers: shared pool option ~8% infra cost uplift; dedicated pools ~28% uplift for small installs, but discounts with larger commit.
Carlos (Sales): customers with annual committed spend >$500k likely ok with dedicated pools as a paid option. smaller customers would prefer shared pools.
Evie (Legal): also flag data residency: if dedicated pools are in customer VPC, we need the Private deployment flows. mention KMS/HSM and logging in the template.
Alice (PM): next steps: - Ben to prototype priority tag router + metric emitter (2 sprints) - Dana & Carlos to run pricing sensitivity and pilot candidate outreach - Evie to draft addon amendment - I'll write launch checklist and sales FAQ.
Ben (Eng): ack. I'll push a short design doc by EOW: includes fallback policy pseudocode and a small config snippet: 
```
priority_addon:
  enabled: true
  mode: shared_warm_pool # or dedicated_pool
  vip_tag: "x-priority"
  fallback: allow_fallback_to_standard:true
```
Alice (PM): love it. keep the config minimal.
Carlos (Sales): can we make the addon name less opsy? customers don't like cryptic names. suggestions: "Priority Delivery", "Fastlane", "Guaranteed QOS".
Dana (Finance): poll in the pilot: see which name lifts conversion.
Evie (Legal): and include clear language about "best-effort" during force majeure.
Alice (PM): thanks team — logging this as thread for roadmap item. will add to initiative board with dependencies and tentative launch quarter Q3. :rocket:
Ben (Eng): quick note — telemetry schema needs a tag for addon_version. otherwise credit calc is messy.
Frank-bot: reminder: weekly infra meeting moved to Tue 10am for prototype sync.
Carlos (Sales): pinging potential pilot customer Y to confirm interest. will update. :phone:
Alice (PM): end of thread.
